text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm putting together a tiny docs PR: 'Low-latency micro-batching + quantized models (FAQ)'. Goal: short guidance + 2 SDK snippets (Java + Rust) + a short migration note. Looking for a reviewer and someone to sanity-check links to quant profiles.

aj: Scope? Keep it as an FAQ or full example page?

maria: FAQ section under Optimize Toolkit -> Best Practices. One para about when to prefer micro-batching vs single-request streaming, one para on kv-prefetch tradeoffs with quantized weights, plus two tiny snippets. No big diagrams.

tim: Happy to review. Can I see the snippets before PR? I want to test the Rust one on a quantized Llama-2-13B Q4 run.

sara: I can own the Java SDK snippet and check link targets (quant-profiles, batching policies). Also will ensure we don't reference deprecated SDK params.

maria: Awesome — draft here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/XXXXX (placeholder). Key checklist: 1) short description, 2) migration note (how defaults changed), 3) snippets small (<12 lines), 4) add cross-ref to /optimize/quant-profiles.


# Rust snippet (tim volunteered to test):

tim: Proposed minimal Rust example for micro-batching + soft kv prefetch off (for tiny memory when quantized):

```rust
// pseudocode - using redwood-sdk-rs (experimental)
let client = RedwoodClient::new("$API_KEY");
let req = GenerationRequest::builder("short prompt")
    .model("llama-2-13b-q4_ks")
    .batching_policy(BatchingPolicy::Micro { max_batch_tokens: 512 })
    .kv_prefetch(false) // avoid extra mem with Q4 kernels
    .max_tokens(64)
    .build();
let resp = client.generate(req).await?;
println!("{}", resp.text);
```

maria: Good start. Add a short comment about latency vs throughput tradeoff and a note: "test with representative short-sequence workload".

aj: One nit — don't call the model name out as canonical in the snippet; use `model("<model-name>")` to avoid future churn.

tim: Updated snippet: use placeholder model field, and added comment about testing short-seq vs long-seq.


# Java snippet (sara):

sara: Tiny Java snippet for our Java SDK (sync):

```java
// pseudocode - redwood-java-client
RedwoodClient client = new RedwoodClient(System.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"));
GenerationRequest req = GenerationRequest.builder()
    .model("<model-name>")
    .maxTokens(64)
    .batching(BatchingPolicy.micro(256)) // micro-batch to reduce per-token overhead
    .kvPrefetch(false) // helps on quantized backends with limited RAM
    .build();
GenerationResponse resp = client.generate(req);
System.out.println(resp.getText());
```

sara: Also adding a one-liner about enabling `prefetch` for batched large-seq workloads.

maria: Perfect. Two doc-edge checks before PR: 1) ensure the quant-profiles link points to stable anchor (quant-profiles.md#recommendations), 2) add a one-sentence migration note: "older examples enabled kv-prefetch by default; when moving to quantized kernels, benchmark both settings."

docs-bot: Reminder: docs PRs must include code block linting and samplegen entry if there are new snippets — see CONTRIBUTING.md#samplegen.


aj: I'll run the docs lint locally (prettier + remark) and check the anchors. If we add samplegen metadata, keep filenames namespaced under optimize/microbatch-quant.

tim: I already ran a quick perf smoke: for our short-seq workload, micro-batching (256 tokens, batch size 8) improved tail latency slightly but single-request streaming still wins for 1-3 concurrent users. Adding this as a one-sentence finding in the FAQ.

sara: Link fix: quant-profiles anchor is currently `#profiles-recommendations` (I checked). I'll point the doc to that anchor.

maria: OK I'm going to open a draft PR with those snippets and the checklist. Tagging you all for review. Will mark as `WIP` and request review from @tim @sara @aj.

aj: Thx — will do quick lint pass tomorrow.

tim: I'll run the Rust snippet against the Q4 build and post any adjustments.

sara: I'll add a short migration bullet to the Optimize Toolkit release notes.

maria: Closing loop: draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/12345 (real link once created). Please review by EOD Friday if possible. :rocket:
